segments.text: What are Transformers? Transformers are the architecture behind most modern AI models.
Chat, GPT, Claude, Gemini. Most large language models today are built on some version of the
Transformer. And the big reason they work so well comes down to one idea, attention.
Let's build the intuition from scratch. Imagine the sentence. The animal didn't cross the street
because it was too tired. What does the word it refer to? The street or the animal? A human
looks at the surrounding words and understands that it refers to the animal. Transformers
do something similar. Instead of processing each word in isolation, they look at how every
Every token relates to the others.
That mechanism is called self-attention.
Let's say the model is processing the word it.
Which previous words should I pay attention to in order to understand what it means?
Maybe animal gets a high attention score, street gets a lower score, tired also matters.
The model combines all of that context into a better representation of the word and it
does this for every token.
Now here's where it gets powerful.
Transformers don't just use one attention pattern, they use multiple attention heads.
One head might learn relationships between subjects and pronouns.
Another might focus on grammar.
Another might connect cause and effect. Another might track long-range dependencies.
Together, these heads let the model build a richer understanding of the text.
But attention alone isn't enough. Words also need position,
because dog bites man and man bites dog contain the same words,
but obviously mean very different things.
So transformers also include positional information.
That tells the model where each token appears in the sequence.
Now let's zoom out.
A transformer is built from layers. Inside each layer, you usually have self-attention.
A feed-forward neural network, normalization, and residual connections.
The output of one layer becomes the input to the next, layer after layer.
The model builds more abstract representations.
Early layers might learn simple syntax.
Deeper layers can capture meaning, relationships, patterns, and more complex concepts.
Now how does this become chat GPT?
During training, a language model sees enormous amounts of text.
Then it repeatedly plays one game, predict the next token.
For example, the capital of France is, the model might assign high probability to
Paris.
If it predicts badly gradient descent, adjusts the model's weights, then it tries again.
After doing this across massive data sets, the Transformer learns statistical patterns
about language, facts, code, reasoning, style, and many other things.
Now one reason Transformers became such a big deal is parallelism.
Older architectures like RNN's process sequence is more step by step.
Transformers can process many tokens in parallel during training.
That makes them much easier to scale across huge GPU clusters.
And scale turned out to matter a lot.
More data.
More compute.
More parameters.
more layers. That's how we went from the original transformer paper to models with hundreds of billions of parameters.
So the easiest way to think about a transformer is this. Instead of reading text one word at a time and forgetting what came before,
it constantly asks which parts of this context matter most for understanding what I'm looking at right now.
That attention mechanism repeated across billions of parameters in many layers is one of the core ideas behind modern AI.
